greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you come to set the earth on fire with your love. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you strengthen us in our inner selves through your Spirit. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the hope of every family in heaven and on earth. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.
homily:
There is a particular kind of quiet that settles over a home in the late afternoon. It is the time when the light begins to stretch across the floorboards, when the busyness of the day ebbs away, and when, if you are still, you can almost hear the house breathing. It is in these moments of stillness that we are most vulnerable to the memories that come unbidden. Perhaps it is the sight of a pair of shoes left by the door, or the way a certain shadow falls across a desk, or the sudden, sharp recollection of a laugh that used to fill the hallway. These are not just echoes; they are the heart’s way of reaching back into the light of a life that has been lived, and lived well.

In our first reading today, St. Paul kneels before the Father. He is not standing in a posture of triumph or even of instruction; he is kneeling in a posture of profound, trembling awe. He prays that the Father may 'grant you in accord with the riches of his glory to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner self.' Think of that inner self. It is the hidden room of the heart, the place where we keep our most precious things, the place where we house our deepest griefs and our highest hopes. Paul knows that the world is a place of fire and, at times, of division. He knows that the life of faith is not a gentle stroll through a manicured garden; it is a walk through a world that is often being refined by the fire of Christ’s presence. And so, he asks for strength—not the strength of a soldier, but the strength of one who is 'rooted and grounded in love.'

There is a profound, aching beauty in that image of being 'rooted.' A tree that is rooted does not just stand; it draws life from a source that is hidden beneath the surface. It is fed by the deep, dark, nourishing soil of the earth. When the winds of change blow, when the storms of loss tear through the branches, the tree holds. It holds because it is anchored to something that does not move. Benjamin Vo lived his life with this kind of quiet, sturdy rooting. He was a boy whose mind was always reaching for the sky—the mechanics of flight, the vastness of the clouds, the intricate logic of the code he wrote—but his heart was firmly planted in the love of his family. He was a boy who looked at his own small, finite resources and saw them as seeds to be planted in the lives of others. Remember the way he offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle? It wasn't about the money. It was about the heart of a boy who understood, even at fifteen, that we are here to be a blessing. He didn't need to break the bank to prove his love; the offer itself was a testament to a soul that was already living in the fullness of God.

Alan and Thao, I know the ache of these past four months. I know the way the silence can sometimes feel like a physical weight, a pressure against your chest that makes it hard to breathe. I know the nights when the 'what-ifs' and the 'why-nots' come to visit, when you wonder if there was some hidden detail you missed, some sign you didn't see. Please, let me say this as clearly as I can: you missed nothing. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the ones who held his hand through the world, who fostered his brilliance, who celebrated his joy, and who loved him with a devotion that is a mirror of the Father’s own love. God does not send sickness as a punishment, and he does not hold you to account for the mysteries of a life that was taken too soon. That burden is not yours to carry. It was never yours. You are free, in this moment, to set that stone down. You are not the architects of his end; you are the witnesses to his beautiful, radiant beginning and his enduring, eternal life. You are a family of four, and that is a reality that exists in the heart of God, beyond the reach of any sorrow.

In the Gospel, Jesus speaks of a fire. 'I have come to set the earth on fire, and how I wish it were already blazing!' This is not a fire of destruction. It is the fire of the Holy Spirit. It is the fire of a love so intense, so consuming, that it divides the things that are temporary from the things that are eternal. It is the fire that burns away the dross so that only the gold remains. When Jesus speaks of division, he is speaking of the cost of belonging entirely to God. To be a follower of Christ is to be pulled into a reality that the world often does not understand. It is to love with a depth that makes the world’s priorities seem small and brittle. Benjamin lived in that fire. He lived with a joy that was infectious, a giggle that came whenever he talked about his 'con chim airlines,' a dream that was so pure it became a part of the air he breathed. He wasn't afraid of the fire. He was a boy who was already burning with the light of God’s own curiosity and kindness.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the geometry of this love better than anyone. You know the way the house feels, the way the memories are woven into the very fabric of your life together. You are the one who carries the legacy of his kindness. You are the one who knows that the bond you share with Ben is not a matter of geography or time. It is a matter of the spirit. When you look at the sky, when you think of the planes, when you remember the games you coded together, you are not looking at a past that is gone. You are looking at a future that is waiting. You are a vital part of this family, and your life, too, is a testament to the love that Ben shared. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who sees the beauty in the small things. You are a witness to the world that love is stronger than any distance.

There is a moment in a dream that your father shared—that beautiful, simple moment of waiting in line for ice cream, where Ben was the one who paid. It is a small thing, a mundane, human thing. But in the landscape of grief, it is a mountain of hope. It is a sign that the roles we play, the love we share, the simple, everyday gestures of affection—they do not end. They are gathered up. They are held. They are the currency of the Kingdom of Heaven. When you feel the ache of his absence, remember that he is not lost. He is just waiting in a different line, in a place where the ice cream never melts and the sun never sets. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile, the one that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the fire of God’s love has already accomplished its work in him.

We are living in a time that often feels like a long, cold night. We see the world changing, we feel the ground shifting, and we are tempted to look for security in the things we can control. But Jesus is inviting us to look at the fire. He is inviting us to trust that the heat we feel—the heat of our longing, the heat of our tears—is the heat of his presence. He is not distant. He is the one who is kneeling with you in the silence. He is the one who is holding your hand when the night is at its deepest. He is the one who is whispering to your hearts that you are not alone, that you are not forgotten, and that you are loved beyond all measure.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is not a new set of plans. It is a simple, quiet, doable thing: keep your heart open to the fire. When you feel the ache, do not turn away from it. Let it be the place where God meets you. When you see someone who is struggling, when you see someone who is thirsty, when you see someone who is just trying to make it through the day, remember that they, too, bear the image of the Creator. Reach out to them. Give a little of your time, a little of your heart, a little of your kindness. Not because you have to, but because you are overflowing with the love that Benjamin left behind. You are the stewards of his legacy. You are the ones who keep the well flowing.

Do not be afraid of the future. The same God who held Benjamin in his hand as he looked out at the sky is the same God who holds you today as you look out at your own horizon. He is not a stranger. He is your Father. He knows the exact shape of your heart, he knows the depth of your longing, and he knows how much you miss the one you love. And he is promising you that the story is not over. The reunion is certain. Keep your eyes on the sky. Keep your heart in the light. And remember that he is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the banquet is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may his face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may he give you his peace. Go in the love of Christ.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ.
For all who carry the heavy cross of grief, that they may be consoled by God’s presence and filled with the hope of eternal reunion.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
I kneel before the Father,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named,
that he may grant you in accord with the riches of his glory
to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner self,
and that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith;
that you, rooted and grounded in love,
may have strength to comprehend with all the holy ones
what is the breadth and length and height and depth,
and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge,
so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.Now to him who is able to accomplish far more than all we ask or imagine,
by the power at work within us,
to him be glory in the Church and in Christ Jesus
to all generations, forever and ever.  Amen.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (5b) The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.
Exult, you just, in the LORD;
praise from the upright is fitting.
Give thanks to the LORD on the harp;
with the ten-stringed lyre chant his praises.
R. The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.
For upright is the word of the LORD,
and all his works are trustworthy.
He loves justice and right;
of the kindness of the LORD the earth is full.
R. The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.
But the plan of the LORD stands forever;
the design of his heart, through all generations.
Blessed the nation whose God is the LORD,
the people he has chosen for his own inheritance.
R. The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.
But see, the eyes of the LORD are upon those who fear him,
upon those who hope for his kindness,
To deliver them from death
and preserve them in spite of  famine.
R. The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples:
“I have come to set the earth on fire,
and how I wish it were already blazing!
There is a baptism with which I must be baptized,
and how great is my anguish until it is accomplished!
Do you think that I have come to establish peace on the earth?
No, I tell you, but rather division.
From now on a household of five will be divided,
three against two and two against three;
a father will be divided against his son
and a son against his father, 
a mother against her daughter
and a daughter against her mother,
a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law
and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”

day: Thursday of the Twenty-ninth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!
